_doc: The Actions-minute budget for this repository. Read by
scripts/check_actions_budget.py, which REPORTS the projected month against
`hard_ceiling_minutes` while `enforcement.enabled` is false and FAILS on it
only when that switch is true. It also WARNS, without failing, when the
projection exceeds the `design_target_minutes`, and it FAILS when a workflow
file has no entry here, when an entry's crons or job count no longer match
the workflow, or when the projection changes without this file changing.
WHY A CAP AND NOT A HOPE. This repository is now PUBLIC, so standard
runners are free: no minute is billed and no allowance is spent. The cap is
therefore a RECORD of what this tree would cost, recomputed on every run and
still required to match this file -- not a bill. It exists because of
2026-10-18, when the account was refused at runner-assignment: about 2,016
minutes had been consumed by the 18th, i.e. about 3,360 in a month, against
an allowance of 2,000, and the owner cannot buy more (no USD access from
Nepal). The reserve below is the margin that kept that from recurring while
the minutes did bill.
HOW THE NUMBERS WERE CHOSEN. `p95_minutes` is PER JOB, and it is the
calibration from the measured October consumption, not the workflow
timeout -- a budget built on timeouts flags everything and gets ignored.
`max_runs_per_day` is what the workflow is ALLOWED to produce, not what
GitHub's scheduler actually delivers: GitHub `schedule` is demonstrably
not a clock here (crons aimed at 07:50 and 19:50 Nepal time landed near
12:55 and 23:01), so an hourly cron does not mean 24 runs a day.
MEASURED OCTOBER, per the account audit: daily-news 862 min over 141
runs, drift-canary 393 over 41 (4 jobs each), digest-prebuild 233 over
26 (2 jobs each), breaking-monitor 225 over 140, academic-result 179
over 84, digest-watchdog 124 over 124. 18 days, hence x30/18 for a month.
THIS IS AN ESTIMATE, NOT THE METER. The token cannot read the billing
endpoints (it lacks the `user` scope), so no endpoint can be asked what
was actually spent. budget-sentinel.yml is the runtime half: it measures
real job durations instead of declaring them.
TWO NUMBERS, DELIBERATELY SEPARATE, NEVER CONFUSED (2026-10-20).
`design_target_minutes` (1,400) is an ASPIRATION: what this repository
should cost. It is REPORTED, never ENFORCED -- the checker WARNS on it and
budget-sentinel.yml reports it, and neither refuses anything on it. Refusing
at 1,400 would stop work while 600 minutes of allowance were still unspent,
and the owner would lose digests he could have had. `hard_ceiling_minutes`
(1,800) is the number every level is a fraction of: the included allowance
(2,000) minus `budget_reserve_minutes` (200). budget-sentinel.yml reports
80%, 90% and 100% of it and, ONLY while `enforcement.enabled` is true, files
an issue at 80%, adds the `budget-freeze` label at 90% and FAILS at 100%.
While it is false all three levels are report-only: nothing is filed,
labelled, notified or shed. The Worker's runtime quota reports on the ceiling
and refuses on it only in the armed state -- which this file is not in.
ENFORCEMENT IS A SWITCH, SEPARATE FROM THE ARITHMETIC (2026-10-25).
`enforcement.enabled` says whether anything may ACT on the hard ceiling: the
Worker's dispatch refusal, the sentinel's issue/freeze/failure, and the static
check's ceiling failure. It is false because this repository is now PUBLIC,
where standard runners are free: acting on a minute nobody is billed for buys
nothing and can only cost a digest. NOTHING ELSE CHANGED. The numbers above are
untouched and still checked; the Worker still charges every dispatch to its KV
month record and still reports `budget{}` on `?health=1`; and the projection is
still recomputed on every run and still has to match this file. Only the acting
is off.
Set `enabled` back to true to re-arm it -- the repository could go private again.
THE STATIC CHECK FOLLOWS THE SAME SWITCH (2026-10-28). While `enabled` is
false, check_actions_budget.py prints the ceiling as REPORT-ONLY and exits 0
even when the projection is above it, because a free minute cannot be over
budget. It still FAILS on a workflow with no entry here, on crons or job
counts that no longer match the workflow, and on a recorded projection that
disagrees with the tree: those protect the truth of this record, not the
height of the number. Flip `enabled` to true and the old ceiling failure
returns unchanged.
WHY 200 AND NOT MORE. 200 is the measured model error kept as margin. The
last comparable month came in 282 minutes (9.2%) above its own model (3,360
measured vs 3,078 modelled), and the reserve is ~71% of that. That argument
was written when the model was BELOW the ceiling; it is kept because the
reason for the margin has not changed -- what changed is that the model is
now honest, and 2,229 is above 1,800. See the next paragraph rather than
quietly re-deriving a reserve that would make the arithmetic look better.
2,229 IS THE HONEST MODEL AND IT IS OVER THE HARD CEILING BY 429.
The number used to be 1,791, and 1,791 was achieved partly by billing
drift-canary at 2.4 minutes per job -- see the 2026-11-03 note below the
projection fields. Replacing that with the measured 17.0 took it to 2,229.
NO NUMBER WAS NUDGED TO MAKE IT FIT: the hard ceiling stayed at 1,800, the
design target stayed at 1,400 and the cron stayed daily. While
`enforcement.enabled` is false the check PRINTS the overage and exits 0,
because standard runners are free on a public repository; the two ways to
close the 429 are (a) re-declare the allowance and the ceiling upward, which
means editing deploy/cloudflare-worker.js and budget-sentinel.yml together
since the Worker enforces the same constants, or (b) reduce volume -- at 17
minutes a run, daily is 510 and a weekly cron would be ~74, which fits with
7 minutes to spare. Neither has been done: this is the owner's call, recorded
here so the gap is visible instead of absorbed.
WHAT THE OLD 1,746 PARAGRAPH SAID, KEPT AS HISTORY. 1,746 replaced the stale
3,138 as the figure this tree computes, after three changes on 2026-10-19/20:
the cron cuts plus the job merges recorded per-workflow below (drift-canary to
ONE job on ONE cron, digest-prebuild to ONE job with no schedule, academic-result
24 -> 2 firings, breaking-monitor 4 -> 1); narrowing the prebuild poll from
20x15s to 5x6s (prebuild p95 4.5 -> 1.5, 270 -> 90 a month); and moving the
empty-digest retry ladder off digest-watchdog.yml's 72-a-day GitHub cron onto
the Worker's own minute grid (watchdog 7 -> 2 runs a day, 210 -> 60). Those
cuts were real and are still in force; only the drift-canary p95 in that sum
was wrong, which is what took 1,746/1,791 to 2,229.

enforcement.reason: public repository - standard runners are free
enforcement._re_enable: Flip `enabled` to true to put the hard-ceiling refusal back, and flip BUDGET_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED in deploy/cloudflare-worker.js with it -- the Worker cannot read this file at runtime, so Check 21 fails if the two disagree.
enforcement._visibility_probe: The Worker asks GitHub for `.private` at most once every 6 hours (KV key `budget:visibility`) and force-disables enforcement while the answer is public, whatever `enabled` says. A probe that cannot answer (no token, non-200, no boolean `private`) is NOT read as public: `enabled` decides, which is why the switch must still work on its own.

budget-sentinel.yml.why: The guard's own cost, budgeted like everything else -- a detector that is not in the budget is the first thing to make the budget a lie. One job a day; 2 minutes rather than 1 because it makes one API call per run in its window (~200), and the step prints its own elapsed time.

daily-news.yml.why: The most expensive single thing here: one job, but a real agent run. Two schedule firings plus the Worker's dispatches. 8 -> 6 runs a day on 2026-10-19, when Drift Canary's two daily dry-run dispatches were removed. AT 1,098 MINUTES THIS IS 53% OF THE WHOLE BUDGET AND 2.4x THE ARCHITECT'S 570 TARGET, and it is the ONLY line that can close the remaining 676-minute gap: 570 implies ~3.1 runs a day at the measured 6.1 minutes, i.e. HALF the current volume. That is not a cron to trim -- it is the digest build, its prebuild dispatch and its fallback/re-fire ceiling, so cutting it trades a delivery guarantee for minutes. Left at 6 deliberately; recorded here so the trade is visible rather than made quietly.

drift-canary.yml.why: ONE job per run since 2026-10-19 (B): docs-lint, drift-canary, the live-parser canary and the stdlib suite now share one job on one daily cron, so a run costs 1 billed minute minimum instead of 4, and a single job `timeout-minutes` replaces the four separate budgets (5+60+12+10). The '17 3 * * *' cron went in the same change, so 3 runs a day became 1. That timeout is 46 since 2026-11-03, raised from 25 because 25 was BELOW the measured work rather than generous. A timeout is a ceiling, not a cost, and it is NOT an input to the projection. `p95_minutes` is 17.0 SINCE 2026-11-03, and the history matters because the old value was not a measurement at all: 2.4 was October's 393 min over 41 runs (9.6 min per RUN) divided by the FOUR jobs that workflow used to have, carried over untouched when the four merged into one -- so a one-job run was billed a quarter of itself, the line projected 72 instead of 510, and the total advertised 9 spare minutes under a ceiling this tree is 429 over. 17.0 is the measured suite work of a full `python tests/ci_local.py --extra` run on 2026-11-03: 1,002.9 s = 16.7 min, rounded up to whole billed minutes (a second full run the same day took 581.9 s = 9.7 min; the slow run is used because p95 is the pessimistic tail, the 573 s -> 286 s `workflow_lint` spread being the whole difference). It is a FLOOR, not padding: the job also runs checkout, node, the CLI install, the typo sweep, the live parser canary, the PKB note and the hold commit, none of which tests/ci_local.py can time. 17.0 x 1 job x 1 run x 30 days = 510 a month.

digest-prebuild.yml.p95_reduced_since_measurement: 233 min over 26 runs is 9.0 min per run in October, taken with the two-job shape and a 20x15s poll; the second job was deleted on 2026-10-19 and the poll narrowed to 5x6s on 2026-10-20, so the run is checkout plus the artifact reads. 1.5 is still an ESTIMATE -- budget-sentinel.yml has not timed a run since the job merge -- and this field exists so the reduction is ARGUED here rather than inherited silently.
digest-prebuild.yml.why: No schedule: dispatched by the Worker, so it is absent from any cron arithmetic and still a real cost. ONE job per run since 2026-10-19 (A): the `dispatch` job that dialled daily-news.yml and then waited up to 45 minutes for it is gone, and the build now hands the seal its OWN run id as its last step, so nothing watches anything. `p95_minutes` was carried over from the two-job measurement at 4.5 while the seal still polled; NARROWED TO 1.5 on 2026-10-20 once the poll went from 20x15s to 5x6s. The hand-off step that dials the seal is gated `success()` and is the build job's LAST step, so the run has already concluded by the time the seal starts and only GitHub's read eventual-consistency remained. The 1.5 is checkout + the artifact reads + the record/supersede work, and it is STILL AN ESTIMATE: no run has been timed since the job merge, so budget-sentinel.yml confirms or refutes it. See `p95_reduced_since_measurement`, which is what stops that sentence from being only a sentence.

breaking-monitor.yml.why: The Worker dispatches it on its own schedule and is the sensor; the cron is the late-tolerant backstop and was cut from 4 firings a day to 1 on 2026-10-19 (8 -> 5 runs a day). A dead Worker is now noticed within ~24 hours rather than 6.

academic-result.yml.why: Worker-dispatched on detection; the cron is the dead-man's backstop and was cut from 24 firings a day to 2 on 2026-10-19 (09:02 and 15:02 Nepal time, inside TU office hours). KNOWN LIMIT: the measured 4.7 runs a day was the congested hourly backstop plus rare result dispatches, and the split cannot be recovered from the aggregate -- so this entry declares the 2 scheduled firings and lets budget-sentinel.yml see any dispatch-driven spike rather than assuming one here.

delivery-selftest.yml.why: MANUAL DISPATCH ONLY -- no schedule, no repository_dispatch, so it costs nothing until a human asks for it, and `max_runs_per_day: 1` is a ceiling on that asking rather than a forecast. It is budgeted anyway because the checker fails a workflow file with no entry here, and because 'it is only manual' is exactly how an unbudgeted job becomes an unbudgeted habit. One job: checkout, setup-python, one script. The script's own work is bounded by SMTP_TIMEOUT_SEC (20s) and the Bot API's 10s timeout, so 1.0 minute is the honest shape, not the 10-minute job timeout.

ledger-repair.yml.why: MANUAL DISPATCH ONLY -- no schedule, no repository_dispatch. It exists to retire one historical false row in KV `digest:ledger` (2026-10-26 evening), and a second run finds nothing to do. `max_runs_per_day: 1` is a ceiling on human asking, not a forecast. Budgeted because the checker fails a workflow file with no entry, and because 'it is one-off' is how an unbudgeted job becomes an unbudgeted habit. ONE job: checkout, setup-python and one script that makes two KV round trips (GET, then PUT + read-back), each bounded at 30s -- 0.5 minute is the shape of that work, not the 5-minute job timeout.

digest-watchdog.yml.why: TWO runs a day since 2026-10-20, down from seven. The 17,32,47 empty-digest retry ladder was removed from this workflow's `schedule:` and moved onto the Worker's own minute grid (SCHED_LADDER_PHASE in deploy/cloudflare-worker.js), which dials this workflow with ladder_only=true only when state/digest_retry.json says a retry is due -- at most twice a day, and those land inside the same pair. Billed at ONE job per run throughout: `watchdog` is gated to the 04/16 firing and never rides the ladder. The 124 minutes measured in October were the ladder's 72 daily minute-long checks plus the pair; that is the cost this change removes.
